styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Roman citadel, amphitheatre and the old downtown.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Falafel, mansaf and sweet shops on Rainbow Street.

styles.label: Budget
styles.blurb: Cheap eats, cheap buses and free viewpoints.

stays.why: Walk to the Citadel, Roman Theatre and Hashemite Plaza. Cheapest base and best for street food.
Quiet, leafy streets near Rainbow Street cafés. Good middle ground between old and new Amman.
Upscale, calm and close to restaurants and malls. Best if you want quiet nights and easy taxis.
Modern business district with hotels and cafés. Central for the BRT and short rides to most sights.

food: Start with falafel and hummus at a downtown shop; a full plate is often under 3 JOD.
Try mansaf, the national dish of lamb cooked in yogurt, for a bigger sit-down meal.
Rainbow Street and Jabal Amman have cafés and sweet shops; knafeh is the local dessert to order.
Cheap eats: shawarma, falafel and fuul sandwiches for about 1–3 JOD.
Book a popular restaurant for Friday lunch; many places are busy and some close early on Fridays.
more_time: Add a day trip to Jerash for Roman ruins; check bus and tour options on the day.
Swap an afternoon for Madaba and Mount Nebo, known for mosaics and views.
Float in the Dead Sea: a long half-day trip; check transport and prices on the day.

recommend.why: Two nights cover the Citadel, the Roman Theatre and downtown food, with time for a day trip.

month_notes: Jan: cold and wet, highs near 12°C. Pack a warm layer and a rain jacket.
Feb: still cool and rainy, around 14°C. Good for indoor sights and museums.
Mar: milder at 17°C with fewer rainy days. Comfortable for walking downtown.
Apr: warm and mostly dry, highs near 23°C. One of the best months to visit.
May: hot and dry, around 28°C. Sightsee early and rest in the afternoon.
Jun: hot at 31°C with no rain. Carry water and use taxis between sights.
Jul: peak heat, 33°C. Plan indoor time midday and go out in the evening.
Aug: as hot as July, 33°C. Same advice: early starts and shade.
Sep: still hot at 31°C but cooling slightly. Evenings get pleasant.
Oct: warm at 26°C with little rain. Great for walking and day trips.
Nov: cooler at 20°C with some rain. Bring a light jacket.
Dec: cold and wet, highs near 15°C. Pack warm clothes and check the forecast.

climate_guide.summary: Mediterranean-style climate: hot, dry summers and cool, wet winters. Spring and autumn are the best times to visit.

items.title: Best time: April to May and October
items.text: Warm days around 23–28°C with little rain. Ideal for the Citadel and walking downtown.

items.title: Hot, dry summer (June to September)
items.text: Highs of 31–33°C and almost no rain. Sightsee early morning and evening; rest indoors at midday.

items.title: Wet winter (December to February)
items.text: Highs of 12–15°C with 6–9 rainy days a month. Bring a warm layer and a rain jacket.

items.title: Rain is seasonal
items.text: Most rain falls from November to March. Summer months are almost completely dry.

items.title: Cool nights year-round
items.text: Evenings drop fast, especially in winter. A light jacket helps in spring and autumn.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light clothes and sunscreen for summer; warm layers and a rain jacket for winter. Comfortable shoes for steep, hilly streets.

transit.best: Use Uber, Careem or taxis for most trips; the BRT bus is the cheap backbone.

modes.text: No metro or tram in Amman. Don't plan around rail.
The BRT bus network is the fast backbone, about 0.610 JOD a ride. City buses are cheap but often Arabic-only; pay exact fare or swipe a Visa or MasterCard.
Yellow and grey taxis use meters; most trips in town stay under 2–5 JOD. Uber and Careem work well, with core rides about 1–4 JOD.
Driving is common but traffic is heavy. Rental desks are at the airport and in town.
Walking is patchy: steep hills, missing sidewalks and few crossings. Plan some rides.
